mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines of 1% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% indicates a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts earnings and growth expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month, without a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate, suggests involuntary layoffs not yet reflected in official unemployment data, foreshadowing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > 0.5% month-over-month AND UNRATE flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS falls > 0.5% month-over-month and UNRATE is flat.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between real retail sales (RSAFS) and personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) with RSAFS growing faster than GDPC1 by at least 0.5% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters signals underreported consumer demand, which, if sustained, should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS - GDPC1 > +0.5% qoq for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS outpaces GDPC1 by > 0.5% qoq for two consecutive quarters.
